project.name: devices
project.description:
Mobile SDK backend (device-channel module): lets a tenant pair a phone (Android today, iOS skeleton - see the separate ios/ and android/ top-level Mobile SDK directories) to the platform and lets a workflow's "Device Control" node queue a command for that device to execute (tap, type text, open an app, take a screenshot). Reuses two already-established cross-module patterns rather than inventing new ones: schema-per-tenant persistence for MobileDevice/DeviceCommand (tenancy), and the ExternalAccountProvider/ChannelAccountLink cross-tenant lookup (tenancy) for resolving which tenant schema a bare device token belongs to on an unauthenticated (no Keycloak JWT) poll/result request - the same posture Twilio's and the workflow webhook's inbound endpoints already use, see DeviceGatewayController's javadoc.
Deliberately polling, not a persistent WebSocket: a phone's OS (Android Doze/App Standby, iOS background execution limits) kills long-lived sockets in the background regardless of what the server offers, so a real mobile automation product (MDM tools, Tasker, etc.) polls or uses platform push (FCM/APNs) - not raw WebSocket - for exactly this reason. Short-interval polling here is the honest, working choice; a push-notification wake-up trigger (to shorten the interval a device needs to poll at) is a reasonable later enhancement, not a compromise hidden as "done."
